# Found You — Photo Metadata Analyzer

> Free, privacy-focused web tool that shows what a photo reveals (location, time, device, people, text) and produces a cleaned copy. The photo itself never leaves the browser: metadata parsing, detection, OCR, blurring and export all run on the user's device.

## What It Does

Found You (formerly Meta Data Insight) extracts hidden metadata from a photo, detects faces, people and objects, recognizes text, lists the facts a stranger could read from it (each with how an attacker would use it), enriches GPS coordinates with place context (disclosed next to the result, switchable off), and lets the user download a safe copy with verified-clean metadata.

## Key Features

- **Metadata extraction**: EXIF, XMP, IPTC and ICC from JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP and HEIC/HEIF; PNG text chunks (tEXt/zTXt/iTXt, e.g. AI-generation prompts). HEIC is decoded locally.
- **Face and object detection**: MediaPipe Tasks Vision — FaceDetector (BlazeFace short-range) for faces, ObjectDetector (EfficientDet-Lite2, COCO labels) for people and objects; the WASM runtime and models are self-hosted. The cleanup option "Faces" blurs each detected face box (padded); people without a detected face are covered with the manual brush.
- **OCR**: Tesseract.js (Russian + English) with region-level bounding boxes; recognized text regions can be blurred. Runtime and language data are self-hosted.
- **Facts**: one section lists what the photo says — the location with the map and nearby places, how and when the photo was taken, people, text, licence plates, QR codes, documents and contacts, and where the file comes from (device, file history with the embedded thumbnail, authenticity) — each with a plain-language "how an attacker uses it" and its details inline; no verdict, no story, no habit inferences; a device-specific recipe for turning geotags off; the raw metadata table behind a button.
- **Licence plates**: candidates are found without a dedicated model — OCR tokens that read like a plate (letters + digits in a wide box) and short alphanumeric tokens on a detected vehicle — and can be blurred with one switch.
- **Content Credentials (C2PA)**: manifest presence is detected by parsing the container (JPEG APP11 JUMBF, PNG caBX, WebP C2PA, HEIC/AVIF uuid); only then the self-hosted c2pa toolkit parses and validates it. The AI fact shows the generator, author, signer, actions and validation result; files without a manifest are labelled honestly as "metadata-only check".
- **Place context**: when the photo carries GPS, rounded coordinates (~11 m) and the capture date/time are sent to the site's own Cloudflare Pages Functions, which proxy Nominatim (address), Open-Meteo (historical weather for the hour of capture), Nager.Date (public holidays, with a static fallback for Uzbekistan) and Overpass (nearby places, likely surveillance cameras). The section states exactly what was sent; a "Do not request place context" switch stops these requests and is remembered. A MapLibre map with OpenStreetMap tiles is shown alongside.
- **Cleanup and export**: re-encoding through canvas removes source metadata; container-level metadata added by the browser (ICC profile, comments) is stripped as well; the exported file is re-parsed and the UI reports "N metadata fields before, 0 left". The "metadata only" preset keeps the original JPEG/PNG picture bytes and only rewrites the container (every metadata segment and anything after the end of the image, such as a Samsung trailer, is dropped). Options: blur detected faces (people without a detected face are covered with the brush), blur OCR text, licence plates, QR codes, documents and contacts, manual brush masks, weaken camera sensor fingerprint (PRNU), anti-reverse-image-search transforms, mirror, downscale, watermark, output format (original/JPEG/PNG/WebP) and quality, neutral filename by default. Where the browser can share files (Web Share API on iOS, Android, macOS Safari) the cleaned copy can go straight to a messenger without touching the gallery.
- **Limits**: 20 MB and 40 megapixels per file; export capped at 40 MP (16 MP on iOS/iPadOS).

## Privacy Architecture

- The image, its pixels, filename and full metadata never leave the device.
- Only 4-decimal rounded coordinates, the capture date/time and (for holidays) the country code ever reach a server — the site's own functions, which forward them to the upstream services (the user's IP is not exposed to those services). The UI discloses this next to the result, and one switch turns it off for good.
- Models, the OCR runtime and the Content Credentials toolkit are served from the site's own domain; no third-party CDN at run time.
- No accounts, no cookies, no analytics or tracking. Strict Content-Security-Policy and other security headers.

## Supported Formats

JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF, BMP, HEIC, HEIF

## Languages

Russian, English, Uzbek. Interface themes: light, dark, auto, high-contrast.

## Technology

React, TypeScript, Vite, MediaPipe Tasks Vision (FaceDetector + ObjectDetector), Tesseract.js, c2pa (Content Credentials), exifr, libheif-js, MapLibre GL. Hosted on Cloudflare Pages with Pages Functions. Source repository: https://github.com/morgunovtech/meta-data

## URL

https://foundyou.morgunov.tech/

## Use Cases

- Check what metadata a phone camera embeds before posting to social media
- Remove GPS location and device information from photos before sharing
- Blur faces, people, text and licence plates in a photo; cover documents with the brush
- Check whether a photo carries Content Credentials and whether it is signed as AI-generated
- Inspect camera and editing-software metadata, including AI-generation prompts in PNG files
- Prepare photos for work chats, listings or publication with a verified-clean copy
